failures.title: BMW B58B30O1 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Coolant System Leaks - expansion tank, hoses, and water pump
items.whatHappens: The B58's complex integrated cooling system uses plastic fittings and quick-release couplers that can become brittle due to heat cycling. Many owners report unexplained coolant loss, often traced to a faulty expansion tank cap, cracked hoses, or a failing electric water pump. The water pump has a high workload and is prone to failure, though less common than on the N55. If ignored, coolant loss can lead to overheating and, in extreme cases, head gasket failure.
items.repairVsReplace: Water pump and thermostat replacement is a straightforward (£400-£800) repair at an independent specialist. If the engine has overheated due to prolonged coolant loss, head gasket failure may justify a full replacement unit. → Read our full /failures/coolant-system-failure guide

items.title: Oil Filter Housing Gasket Leaks
items.whatHappens: The oil filter housing gasket is a known wear point on the B58, with oil seeping from the housing where it meets the block. In some cases, oil can contaminate the cooling system via the integrated oil-coolant heat exchanger, reducing cooling efficiency and accelerating coolant system degradation.
items.repairVsReplace: Gasket replacement is a moderate-cost repair (£300-£600) at an independent BMW specialist. Catch it early; if oil and coolant have mixed extensively, the cooling system may require a full flush and the oil cooler may need replacement.

items.title: PCV Valve Integration Failure
items.whatHappens: The B58 integrates the PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) valve into the cylinder head cover - a sealed unit that cannot be serviced individually. When the PCV diaphragm fails, crankcase pressure rises, leading to oil leaks from seals and gaskets, increased oil consumption, and rough idle.
items.repairVsReplace: The entire cylinder head cover must be replaced (£400-£800) as the PCV valve is non-serviceable. This is a known design compromise; budget for it on higher-mileage B58B30O1 units.

failures.goodYearsLine: The B58B30O1 is the TU (Technical Update) variant introduced from 2019, featuring a revised crankcase for better balance, split-cooling circuits, and increased fuel pressure (350 bar). Post-2020 units received an updated oil pump design addressing earlier plastic rotor housing concerns. Timing chain failure is not a widespread issue on the B58, unlike the N47 and N57 - the chain is considered a lifetime component, though inspection at 200,000 km (124,000 miles) is recommended.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the B58B30O1
variants.intro: The B58B30O1 is a Specific engine code - it identifies the 3.0-litre high-output B58 Technical Update (TU) engine used in G-chassis M Performance models from 2019 onward. Unlike Family pages that cover multiple sub-codes, this page is dedicated to the exact B58B30O1 tune. Where to find your engine code: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible from the driver's side of the engine bay. It is also listed on the V5C registration document (logbook) under the "Engine number" field - the code appears as part of the full engine number (e.g. B58B30O1xxxxxx). For BMW models, the VIN decoder (available via BMW's parts system or online VIN decoders) will also confirm the engine code from the vehicle's build sheet. Commonly confused codes: | Engine Code | What it is | Why it's confused | |---|---|---| | B58B30M0 | 326 hp (240 kW) B58 variant used in earlier 340i, 540i, X5 40i | Lower-output B58 with different ECU calibration and intake plumbing | | B58B30M1 | 382 hp variant used in Toyota Supra and certain BMW applications | Similar power output but different ECU mapping and emissions hardware | | B58B30O0 | Earlier O-series B58 used in X3 M40i (2018-2019) | Pre-TU version with different cooling system layout | Why fitting the wrong revision matters: Installing a B58B30M0 or B58B30O0 ECU or engine management calibration into a B58B30O1 host will cause DME mismatch errors and drivability issues. The B58B30O1 uses 350 bar fuel pressure (up from 200 bar on earlier B58s) and split-cooling circuits - swapping in an earlier B58 without the correct fuel system and cooling components will result in poor performance and potential engine damage.

relatives.description: the B58 replaced the N55 from 2015 onward, and the N55 was a fine engine in its own right, but the B58's closed-deck block, integrated exhaust manifold, and higher fuel pressure make it a significantly more robust foundation for both stock and tuned applications.

BMW's latest B58 evolution (introduced in certain models from 2022) features further cooling improvements and a revised valvetrain. While the B58B30O1 remains current across many models, the TU2 is gradually rolling out in newer G-series cars.

BMW supplies the B58B30O1 (and its M1 variant) to Toyota for the Supra. The physical engine is identical, though the ECU and exhaust tuning differ. If you're a Supra owner looking for replacement information, many of the same B58B30O1 facts apply - but always confirm the exact code on your engine.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement B58B30O1 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used B58B30O1 can make financial sense for lower-value host vehicles or where the original engine has suffered a non-catastrophic failure (e.g. water pump failure caught early). However, used units should come with documented service history and proof of coolant system maintenance - the B58's cooling system complexity means an engine that has overheated is a high-risk purchase. Avoid early 2019-2020 units without evidence of the revised oil pump (post-2020) unless the price reflects the risk. Link once:

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A properly reconditioned B58B30O1 addresses the engine's known weak points: new water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, oil filter housing gasket, PCV valve/cylinder head cover, and VANOS solenoids. This is the right call for most M340i, M440i, and X3 M40i owners - the host vehicle value typically justifies the £3,800-£6,000 supply cost, and a 12-24 month warranty provides peace of mind on a complex modern engine. Link once:

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full B58B30O1 rebuild is justified for high-value hosts (X5, X7, 8 Series, Z4 M40i) or where the engine has suffered catastrophic failure (hydrolock, head gasket failure, bottom-end damage). An upgraded rebuild should include forged pistons, upgraded rod bearings, and a strengthened oil pump - particularly relevant for owners planning tuning or track use. Rebuild costs (£5,000-£8,000 supply-only) are significant but still below the cost of a new OEM crate engine. Link once:

Used: from £2,000 - only with proof of cooling system maintenance and service history. Reconditioned: from £3,800 - the recommended choice for most road cars. Rebuilt: from £5,000 - ideal for high‑value vehicles or performance builds.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the B58B30O1 and not another B58 variant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, visible from the driver's side of the engine bay. It also appears on the V5C registration document under 'Engine number' (e.g. B58B30O1xxxxxx). You can also use a BMW VIN decoder (available online) to extract the engine code from the vehicle's build sheet. Common confusion: B58B30M0 (326 hp), B58B30M1 (382 hp), and B58B30O0 (pre‑TU) have different ECU calibrations and cooling/hardware differences. Fitting the wrong engine variant without corresponding ECU and component swaps will cause drivability issues.

mainEntity.name: What is the expected lifespan and mileage of a B58B30O1?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, a B58B30O1 is capable of 150,000-200,000+ miles without major internal issues. Many owners report trouble‑free running beyond 120,000 miles when coolant system components and the PCV system are replaced proactively at the correct intervals. Key maintenance: replace water pump and thermostat at 80,000 miles; check oil filter housing gasket; replace cylinder head cover (PCV) if oil consumption increases. The engine is considered robust and is often modified beyond 500 hp with supporting mods. The rear‑mounted timing chain is not a common failure point - unlike BMW's N47/N57 diesels.
